summary: DS4-R1/R2 substantially improved the delivery: init now plans @angular/forms and a real compiled TestBed suite runs successfully. Two correctness gaps remain: the compatibility preflight can preserve a Forms range from a different Angular major, and the suite does not exercise formControlName for select, checkbox, and radio group or an attempted change from a disabled radio option.

findings.title: Validate @angular/forms against the supported Angular major before preserving it
findings.detail: The init plan preserves any declared @angular/forms range, but the preflight names and Angular-major comparison omit it. A workspace with @angular/core 22 and @angular/forms 21 therefore passes and keeps Forms 21, yielding incompatible Angular framework packages. Include @angular/forms in the compatibility checks and Angular-major consistency validation, and add fixtures proving a mismatched declared Forms range blocks rather than being preserved.

findings.title: Complete per-control FormControlName and disabled-option interaction coverage
findings.detail: The planned TestBed contract calls for [formControl] and formControlName coverage for each control. The new suite uses formControlName only for switch; select, checkbox, and radio group are tested only with [formControl]. It also labels the radio test as ignoring a disabled option but only asserts its disabled DOM property. Add formControlName hosts/interactions for the remaining three controls and dispatch an attempted change on the disabled radio, asserting neither the FormControl nor valueChange changes.

evidence.command: corepack yarn workspace @code2youlabs/angular test && corepack yarn workspace @code2youlabs/angular check && git diff --check 6e2aecb 481b5bd
evidence.result: passed; 32 CLI tests and 4 compiled TestBed tests

evidence.description: The generated dependency plan now adds @angular/forms, preserving an existing declared range.
@angular/forms is absent from both the checked package names and the Angular-major consistency set.
Only NamedSwitchHost uses formControlName; the radio disabled-option assertion does not attempt an interaction.
